# Agrigate — Firmware 

# What Agrigate is

Agrigate is a seeding monitoring system made by Agriwelt. It watches the seed and fertilizer flow in every row of a seed drill or planter and raises an alarm when a row stops, falls behind or sows wrong. It has two parts:

- **The gateway.** A small unit in the cab, connected to the sensor line of the seeder. It reads every sensor on the line and passes what it reads to the tablet by Bluetooth. It has no screen of its own. In the app it is called the **“Bridge”**.
- **The Hectare app** on an iPad or iPhone. It shows the rows, judges them, raises the alarms, keeps the statistics and sets up the gateway and the sensors.

> **IMPORTANT**
>
> **This is a pre-release version.** The gateway and the app are still changing. These pages describe only what the app and the gateway do today. A function that is not described here should not be relied on.

## What replaces what

| With a Hectare monitor | With Agrigate |
| --- | --- |
| The monitor in the cab, wired to the sensor line | The gateway in the cab, wired to the sensor line |
| The monitor's screen and buttons | The Hectare app on an iPad or iPhone, linked to the gateway by Bluetooth |
| The monitor's buzzer | The tablet's speaker — the alarm sounds through the tablet |

The seed sensors, the HUB-8 hub and the tramline actuators on the seeder are the same Agriwelt devices that work with the Hectare monitors. The app shows them the way the Hectare monitors do: the same bar colours, the same alarm window, the same table and statistics.

## What it does today

- **Seed and fertilizer rows.** One bar per row, in seeds per second (Flow) or seeds per metre (Hybrid, Precision). See [The rows screen](rows-screen.md).
- **Alarms by row number.** A silent, clogged or faulty sensor, a row that does not sow, a row below or above the rate, doubles and skips. See [The alarm window](alarm-window.md).
- **Statistics of five fields** — area, sown and not-sown area, quality. See [Statistics](statistics-screen.md).
- **The devices of the machine** on the HUB-8 hub: hoppers, fans, metering units, work position, tractor inputs, flowmeter. See [HUB-8 inputs](hub8-inputs.md).
- **Tramline**: bouts and rhythm counted by the app, tramline actuators watched. See [Tramline](tramline.md).
- **Updating the gateway** from the app. See [Update the gateway](bridge-update.md).

Every alarm and fault has a three-digit service code. See [How service codes work](codes.md).

> **SEE ALSO**
>
> [What is in the kit](whats-in-the-kit.md) · [What you need](what-you-need.md) · [How the parts connect](how-it-connects.md)


# What is in the kit

An Agrigate system is made of the parts below. The gateway and the app are new; everything on the seeder is the same Agriwelt equipment that works with the Hectare monitors.

| Part | Where it sits | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **The gateway** (**“Bridge”** in the app) | In the cab | Reads every device on the sensor line and talks to the app by Bluetooth. No screen, no buttons to use in work. |
| **The Hectare app** | On an iPad or iPhone in the cab | Shows and judges the rows, raises the alarms, keeps the statistics, sets up the gateway and the sensors. |
| **Seed sensors** | One in the seed tube of every row | Count the seeds of their row. The same sensor type watches fertilizer rows. |
| **HUB-8 hub** (only when needed) | On the seeder | Brings the other devices of the machine onto the sensor line: hopper level, fan speed, metering unit rotation, work position, tractor inputs, flowmeter. |
| **Tramline actuators** (only on machines with tramlining) | On the seeder | Shut the rows of the tramline. |

The seed sensors are connected one after another in a chain. A HUB-8 is needed only for the extra devices of the machine; a seeder with seed sensors alone has none. See [HUB-8 inputs](hub8-inputs.md).

## What this version does not list yet

> **NOTE**
>
> **The cables and the power connection of the kit are not listed in this pre-release version.** Neither are the dimensions and the protection rating of the gateway. Do not wire a gateway from a drawing of another product — ask Agriwelt for the cable set of your machine.

The app is not in the App Store. During the pre-release Agriwelt provides it.

> **SEE ALSO**
>
> [What you need](what-you-need.md) · [How the parts connect](how-it-connects.md) · [Mount and connect the gateway](mount-and-connect.md)


# What you need — iPad or iPhone

## The tablet

| What | Requirement | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Device | iPad or iPhone | The app runs on both. On an iPad the pages sit under a top bar; on an iPhone under the tab bar at the bottom. See [Moving around the app](app-navigation.md). |
| System | iPadOS or iOS 18 or later | The app is built for this version and later. |
| GNSS | An iPad with GNSS (the Cellular models) for **“Hybrid”** and **“Precision”** | Seeds per metre need the ground speed, and the app takes it from the tablet's GNSS. Without it only the Flow mode (seeds per second) is offered. |
| Bluetooth | On, and allowed for the Hectare app | The app reaches the gateway only by Bluetooth. |
| Location | Allowed for the Hectare app (for Hybrid and Precision) | Without it the tablet gives no speed. |

When an iPad gives no GNSS speed, **“Settings”** › **“Products”** says so: **“This iPad gave no GNSS speed — Hybrid and Precision are unavailable. They need an iPad with GNSS (Cellular) and Location allowed.”**

## Set the tablet up so that you hear every alarm

The alarm buzzer plays through the tablet's speaker.

> **IMPORTANT**
>
> **The tablet's volume decides whether you hear an alarm.** The side switch does not silence it, but a volume at zero does. Below 20 % the app shows **“Volume is off”**; with headphones or a Bluetooth speaker connected it shows **“Sound in headphones”**.

| Setting | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Volume | Up. Check it with **“Test sound”** in **“Settings”** › **“Control and Alarms”**. |
| Headphones, external speakers | Not connected. |
| Screen | Kept on: switch on **“Keep screen awake”** in **“Settings”** › **“App”**, or set the tablet's own Auto-Lock to Never. |
| Bluetooth | On. |
| The tablet in the cab | Close to the gateway. Every message about the link asks you to keep the tablet near the gateway. |

The app does not send notifications; Do Not Disturb and Focus do not change the alarm.

> **SEE ALSO**
>
> [First connection to the gateway](first-connection.md) · [Messages over the screen](screen-messages.md)


# How the parts connect

A reading travels this way:

1. **The sensor** in the seed tube counts the seeds of its row.
2. **The sensor line** on the seeder carries the readings of all sensors, the HUB-8 and the tramline actuators to the cab. Every device on the line has its own number; for a seed sensor it belongs to its row.
3. **The gateway** at the cab end of the sensor line asks every device in turn and collects the answers.
4. **Bluetooth** carries them from the gateway to the tablet, about twice a second.
5. **The Hectare app** draws the rows, judges them against the rate and raises the alarms.

## What each part knows

| Part | Knows | Does not know |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sensor | Its own count and its own faults | Anything about the other rows |
| Gateway | Which devices are on the line, in which order, and what each one answers. It keeps the machine profile the app writes to it. | What a HUB-8 input means — a hopper, a fan, the work position. That lives in the app. |
| App | Everything you see: the rate, the control line, the alarms, the statistics, the meaning of every device | — |

So the judgement is made in the app: the alarm delay, the share of rows that must sow, the tolerance — all these are set in the app. See [Control and Alarms settings](settings-control-alarms.md).

## One gateway, one tablet

A gateway talks to one tablet at a time. The app remembers its gateway and connects only to it from then on; when several gateways are in range, it asks which one is yours. See [First connection to the gateway](first-connection.md).

## When the link is lost

When Bluetooth drops, or the gateway stops sending, the app dims the screen — every figure on it is old — and after 3 seconds opens the alarm window **“Bridge link lost”**. The window closes by itself when the gateway answers again. See [code 601](codes-6-gateway-link.md#c601).

> **SEE ALSO**
>
> [What is in the kit](whats-in-the-kit.md) · [Mount and connect the gateway](mount-and-connect.md)


# About the pictures

The pictures in this help are screenshots of the Hectare app in English, taken on an iPad while the app is being built. The app is pre-release: a screen can look slightly different in the version you have.

Most pictures were taken on Agriwelt's test bench, not in a field. You can see that in a few places:

| What you see in a picture | Why |
| --- | --- |
| The yellow capsule **“Volume is off”** at the top of almost every screen | The bench iPad runs with its volume down. In the cab this capsule is a warning that you would not hear an alarm — see [Messages over the screen](screen-messages.md). |
| The word **“bench”** under the speed | The speed is simulated on the bench. In the cab the speed comes from the iPad's GNSS. |
| Rows with faults placed on purpose — a silent row, a blocked row, rows in the tramline | The bench shows every state of a row at once. |
| Very large areas, distances and seed counts on the statistics screen | The bench has been running for many hours. |
| A machine with 7 rows and a working width of 25 m | A bench setting, not a real seeder. |

A few pictures were taken earlier in the development and have been cut to the part that is still current; the explanation under each picture says what to look at.


# Mount and connect the gateway

## Where the gateway goes

The gateway goes **in the cab**, close to where the iPad or iPhone is mounted. The tablet reaches the gateway by Bluetooth: the shorter the distance, the steadier the link. Every message of the app about a lost or broken link asks you to keep the tablet near the gateway.

## What it is connected to

The gateway takes the place of the Hectare monitor at the cab end of the sensor line. It is connected to two things:

- **the sensor line of the seeder** — the same line of seed sensors, HUB-8 and tramline actuators that a Hectare monitor would be connected to;
- **the power of the tractor.**

The sensor line on the seeder itself — the sensors one after another in a chain, the HUB-8 where one is used — is laid out as for a Hectare monitor.

> **IMPORTANT**
>
> **This pre-release version does not describe the cables, the connectors and the power connection of the gateway.** They are not final. Have the gateway connected by Agriwelt or by a fitter who has the cable set and the instructions for your machine. Do not connect the gateway to a socket or a cable meant for another device.

## Check after connecting

The connection is right when the app, with the gateway powered:

1. finds the gateway and connects to it — see [First connection to the gateway](first-connection.md);
2. shows **“Sensors on the bus now”** in **“Settings”** › **“Machine”** with the number of devices you expect on the seeder — see [Set up the machine profile](machine-profile.md);
3. shows every row of the machine on the rows screen, none of them with a red ✕ — see [Bar colours](bar-colours.md).

> **SEE ALSO**
>
> [How the parts connect](how-it-connects.md) · [What is in the kit](whats-in-the-kit.md)


# First connection to the gateway

The app finds the gateway by itself. You only pick it when more than one gateway is in range.

::: steps
1. Power the gateway and keep the tablet in the cab, close to it.

2. Open the Hectare app. The first time, iPadOS asks whether the app may use Bluetooth. Allow it — without Bluetooth the app cannot reach the gateway.

3. The app looks for the gateway. A red capsule in the middle of the screen says **“Looking for the bridge…”**, and the row pages say **“The bridge sends the row count once connected.”**

4. **One gateway in range:** after a few seconds the app connects to it by itself and remembers it. The capsule shows **“Connecting to”** and the name of the gateway, then disappears.

   **Several gateways in range:** the list **“Choose bridge”** opens. Every gateway is a line with its name, its signal bars and its signal strength; the strongest — usually the nearest — is at the top. Tap the gateway of your seeder.

5. The rows of the machine appear on the rows screen. If they do not match your seeder, set the machine profile: [Set up the machine profile](machine-profile.md).
:::

From now on the app connects only to this gateway — it is **“My bridge”** in **“Settings”** › **“Machine”** › **“Bridge”**. If the remembered gateway is not found for a few seconds while others are in range, the list **“Choose bridge”** opens again.

## The bridge section in Settings

**“Settings”** › **“Machine”**, section **“Bridge”**:

| Line | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| The first line | The link: a green dot and the name of the gateway when connected, or what the app is doing, with the signal strength. |
| **“My bridge”** | The remembered gateway, or **“not chosen”**. Tap it to open the list **“Choose bridge”** and pick another one. |
| **“Reconnect”** | Drops the link and connects again to the same gateway. |
| **“Forget bridge”** | The app forgets the gateway, disconnects and offers the list again. It asks first: **“The app will disconnect and let you choose the bridge again.”** — **“Forget”** or **“No”**. |
| **“Bridge firmware”**, **“Hardware revision”** | What the gateway reports about itself. Give them to the service when asked. |
| **“Bridge update”** | See [Update the gateway](bridge-update.md). |
| **“Frames received”**, **“Snapshots”**, **“Dropped frames”** | Counters of the link, for the service. |

> **NOTE**
>
> **A gateway talks to one tablet at a time.** A second tablet near the machine can take the link away from the first. Keep one tablet per machine.

> **SEE ALSO**
>
> [Messages over the screen](screen-messages.md) · [code 601](codes-6-gateway-link.md#c601) · [code 704](codes-7-tablet.md#c704)


# Set up the machine profile

The machine profile tells the gateway which sensors to read and the app how to draw them: how many seed rows, how many fertilizer sensors, and for the Hybrid and Precision modes the working width. It is kept in the gateway, so another tablet connected to the same gateway reads the same profile.

::: steps
1. Open **“Settings”** › **“Machine”**. The section **“Machine profile”** opens at the top.

2. Set **“Rows”** — the number of seed rows — with **−** / **+**.

3. Set **“Fertilizer sensors”** — the number of fertilizer rows with a sensor, or **“none”**.

4. Wait a moment. There is no Save button: after a short pause the app writes the profile to the gateway. The status line under the numbers says **“writing the profile to the bridge…”** and then **“profile written to the bridge at”** with the time.

5. Compare **“Sensors on the bus now”** with what is on the seeder: it counts every device that answers on the sensor line.

6. **Hybrid and Precision only:** set **“Width, cm”** — the working width. **“Row spacing”** under it is worked out by the app: the width divided by the rows of the group.
:::

## When the profile is not written

| The status line says | What it means | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **“bridge busy: seeding under way”** | The gateway does not take a new profile while seed flows. | Stop the seeder and change the number again. |
| **“too many rows for the bridge (up to”** … | The profile is larger than the gateway takes. | Reduce rows or devices. See [code 902](codes-9-setup.md#c902). |
| Any other message with a code | The gateway refused the profile. | See [9xx · Setup answers of the gateway](codes-9-setup.md). |

## Width and statistics

The area and the row spacing come from the width. When the active field already has statistics, a new width asks first: **“Statistics must be erased!”** — **“Yes”** starts the statistics of the active field from zero, **“No”** keeps the old width.

The fertilizer rows come after the seed rows. With fertilizer sensors in the profile, the rows screen shows two bands: seed on top, fertilizer below. See [The rows screen](rows-screen.md).

> **SEE ALSO**
>
> [Number the sensors](sensor-numbering.md) · [Settings — Machine](settings-machine.md)


# Moving around the app — the top bar and the page ring

The app has five pages — **“Rows”**, **“Table”**, **“Statistics”**, **“Field”** and **“Machine”** — and two places that are not pages: the list of **“Alarms”** and the **“Settings”**.

## The top bar on the iPad

::: {.anatomy fig="app-top-bar"}
1. **“Home”** — opens the home screen of the **“Seeding”** tab, by default **“Rows”**. What it opens is set in **“Settings”** › **“App”** › **“Home screen of the Seeding tab”**.
2. **The five pages.** Tap one to open it. The tabs always stand in the same order.
3. **The page on screen** — its tab is lit.
4. **“Alarms”** — the list of the alarms active now. The bell is red with a number when alarms are active: the number of rows, devices and links in alarm. Tap it again to go back to the page you were on.
5. **“Settings”** — tap it again to go back to the page you were on.

The top bar of the iPad, with the page **“Machine”** open.
:::

## The page ring

The pages stand on a ring. Swipe left to go to the next page, right to go back: **“Rows”** → **“Table”** → **“Statistics”** → **“Field”** → **“Machine”** → **“Rows”** again. A swipe must be a clear sideways flick; pressing and dragging on a page (the control line, a row) does not turn the page.

## The tab bar on the iPhone

On an iPhone — and on an iPad when the app has only a narrow part of the screen — the top bar is replaced by a tab bar at the bottom of the screen with four tabs:

| Tab | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| **“Seeding”** | The ring **“Rows”** → **“Table”** → **“Statistics”** → **“Field”**, turned by a swipe; dots under the page show where you are. Tap the lit tab again to go to the home page. |
| **“Machine”** | The page **“Machine”**. |
| **“Alarms”** | The list of active alarms, with the number of alarms on the tab. |
| **“Settings”** | The settings. |

## What lies over every page

Whatever page is open, three things can appear over it: the alarm window ([The alarm window](alarm-window.md)), a red capsule about the link to the gateway and a yellow capsule about the sound ([Messages over the screen](screen-messages.md)).

## The list of alarms

**“Alarms”** shows one line per kind of alarm, with the rows or devices it concerns — the same words as the alarm window. With nothing active it says **“No active alarms”**. Past alarms are not kept.

> **SEE ALSO**
>
> [The rows screen](rows-screen.md) · [Settings](settings.md)


# The rows screen

**“Rows”** is the main working page and, by default, the home page. Every row of the machine is a bar that grows up from the bottom line; its height is the flow of its row, its colour is the judgement.

::: {.anatomy fig="app-rows"}
1. **Sound warning.** Here **“Volume is off”**: an alarm would not be heard. [Messages over the screen](screen-messages.md)
2. **Rate column of the seed band.** On top the actual level of the band, under it the set value (grey), at the bottom the unit: **“s/m”** (seeds per metre, Hybrid and Precision) or **“s/s”** (seeds per second, Flow).
3. **A row in the tramline** — hatched grey. Over row 4 the seed is hatched red: that row sows into the tramline. [Tramline](tramline.md)
4. **Blue bar** — the row sows more than the rate allows (Hybrid and Precision).
5. **The rate line** across every column, with the tolerance lines above and below it (Hybrid and Precision). In Flow a single control line stands here.
6. **Green bar** — the row sows within its tolerance.
7. **Red column** — a sensor that has never answered since power-on blinks bright red. [Bar colours](bar-colours.md)
8. **Yellow bar** — the row sows less than allowed.
9. **Row numbers**, under the columns.
10. **Rate column of the fertilizer band**, here in seeds per second.
11. **Fertilizer band.** With fertilizer sensors in the profile, the seed rows stand in the top band and the fertilizer rows in the bottom band.
12. **The tiles** — speed, area, population and the devices of the machine. [The tiles at the bottom](bottom-tiles.md)

24 seed rows in Precision and 24 fertilizer rows in Flow, on the test bench.
:::

Without fertilizer sensors, up to 20 seed rows stand in one band; more stand in two bands, the first half on top.

## What you can do on this page

| To do this | Do this |
| --- | --- |
| Move the control line (Flow) or the rate (Hybrid, Precision) | Press and hold the digits in the rate column, then drag up or down. The value changes by one step for every 12 points of finger travel (a short move); the highlight goes out 5 seconds after the last touch. In Hybrid and Precision the new rate goes to the gateway when you lift the finger. |
| Open the menu of a row | Press and hold a bar: a loupe names the row under the finger; slide to the row you want and lift the finger. Or tap a band: the eight rows around the finger open large; tap one. [The row menu](row-menu.md) |
| Change the rate by typing it | Tap the **“Population”** or **“Rate”** tile. [The tiles at the bottom](bottom-tiles.md) |
| Go to another page | Swipe left or right, or tap a tab. [Moving around the app](app-navigation.md) |

## When the band is not under control

Control starts when enough rows sow within the norm for 3 seconds running — the share is set in **“Share of seeding rows”**. When seed flows but too few rows are within the norm, the band shows the blinking yellow capsule **“NOT UNDER CONTROL”** with its rows, and the buzzer sounds. No window opens. Check the control line or the rate, and the rows taken off control. [Code 207](codes-2-seeding.md#c207)

While the link to the gateway is down, the whole page is dimmed: the bars show the last reading, not the present.

> **SEE ALSO**
>
> [Bar colours](bar-colours.md) · [Products settings](settings-products.md) · [Control and Alarms settings](settings-control-alarms.md)


# Bar colours and the three reds

In the cab you read the colour, not the text. Every bar of [the rows screen](rows-screen.md) takes one of the looks below.

## The bar itself

| What you see | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| Green bar | The row sows within the norm. |
| Yellow bar | The row sows below the control line (Flow) or below the tolerance band (Hybrid, Precision). |
| Blue bar | The row sows above the tolerance band. Only in Hybrid and Precision. |
| Yellow and blue narrow bars on both sides of a green one | Skips (yellow, left) and doubles (blue, right) of the row. Only in Precision, with **“Skips & doubles”** switched on. |

## The three reds

| What you see | What it means | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Bright red, blinking**, with a red ✕ | The sensor has **never answered** since the gateway was switched on. | Check the sensor's plug and cable. [Code 101](codes-1-row-sensor.md#c101) |
| **Grey background with a red ✕** | The sensor answered, then **went silent**. | Check the sensor's plug and cable. [Code 101](codes-1-row-sensor.md#c101) |
| **Dark red, blinking** | The sensor is there, but **no seed passes it**. | Check the metering unit and the seed tube. [Code 202](codes-2-seeding.md#c202) |

A bright red column blinking with a “?” means that the device on this row's number is not a seed sensor. [Code 106](codes-1-row-sensor.md#c106)

## Other looks

| What you see | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| White column with a black “!” | The row is taken off control: it raises no alarms and does not count toward the share of seeding rows. [The row menu](row-menu.md) |
| Grey hatching | The row is in the tramline and should not sow. [Tramline](tramline.md) |
| Red hatching over the grey | The row sows although it is in the tramline. [Code 206](codes-2-seeding.md#c206) |
| A “?” on top of an empty column | Nothing is known about the row yet. |
| A bar filling slowly with a yellow “?” | The gateway is sending the sensor a new setting, for example a new **“Fraction”**. The rows do this one after another; it takes a few seconds each. |

A sensor that reports a fault — clogged, light struck, faulty — keeps its bar; the reason comes in the alarm window. [1xx · Row sensor faults](codes-1-row-sensor.md)

The same colours are in the built-in help: **“Settings”** › **“App”** › **“Help”** › **“Bar colours and the three reds”**.


# The row menu

The row menu opens from the rows screen — press and hold a bar, slide to the row and lift the finger, or tap a band and then a row — and from the table, by tapping a line. Its title is **“Row”** with the number, or **“Fertilizer · row”** for a fertilizer row. **“Done”** closes it.

## What you see

| Part | What it shows |
| --- | --- |
| The first line | The state of the row in words and colour — for example **“Normal”**, **“Below the line”**, **“Not seeding”**, **“Silent”**, **“Clogged”** — and its rate. |
| **“Precision seeding”** (Precision and Hybrid only) | **“Seeds per metre”**, **“Thousand seeds/ha”**, **“Deviation from rate”**, and in Precision **“Quality, %”**, **“Doubles, %”**, **“Skips, %”**. **“All rows as a table”** opens the table. |
| **“Sensor settings”** | **“Fraction”** — the same value for every row of the group (**“For every seed row.”**). See [Products settings](settings-products.md). |
| **“Information”** | **“Rate”** in seeds per second, **“Control line”**, **“Seeds counted”**, **“Time between seeds”**, **“Sensor”** — what the sensor reports — and **“Last answered”**. |

## What you can do

| To do this | Do this | What happens |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Stop watching a row whose fault you know | **“Disable control”** | The row stays on screen white with a “!”, raises no alarms and does not count toward the share of seeding rows. |
| Watch it again | **“Enable control”** | The row counts again toward control and alarms. |
| Put a new sensor on this row | **“Replace the sensor”** | The numbering sheet opens with this row's number already set. See [Number the sensors](sensor-numbering.md). |
| Switch the product off on this row | **“Product application”** off | The row is treated as a tramline row: no **“Not seeding”**, out of the share of seeding rows, and **“Seeding in tramline”** if it still sows. |

> **IMPORTANT**
>
> **A row taken off control is blind, not quiet.** Nothing about it is watched — not even a lost sensor — until you put it back with **“Enable control”**.

**“Replace the sensor”** is not available while the link to the gateway is down.

> **SEE ALSO**
>
> [The rows screen](rows-screen.md) · [Bar colours](bar-colours.md) · [Table](table-screen.md)


# The tiles at the bottom

Under **“Rows”** and under **“Field”** stands a strip of tiles. Each tile shows one value: a word on top, the value in large figures, the unit, and an icon in a ring. The ring's colour is the state: green — normal, red — alarm (the ring blinks), yellow — attention, grey — no data or not answering.

The strip is there when the machine has something to show in it: a seed group in Hybrid or Precision, or devices on the HUB-8. A Flow machine without devices has no strip.

## What the tiles can show

| Tile | What it shows | A tap opens |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **“Speed”** | The ground speed in km/h from the iPad's GNSS | The speed sheet: the speed and where it comes from |
| **“Area”** | Hectares of the active field | **“Statistics”** |
| **“Population”** | Thousand seeds per hectare (Precision) | The rate sheet |
| **“Rate”** | The set rate in seeds per metre | The rate sheet |
| **“Operating time”** | Hours and minutes of work on the active field | **“Statistics”** |
| **“Field”** | The number of the active field | **“Statistics”** |
| **“Bout”** | The tramline bout, for example “2 / 4” | The bout menu. [Tramline](tramline.md) |
| A device — **“Hopper”**, **“Fan”**, **“Metering unit”**, **“Position”**, **“Flowmeter”** … | Its state in a word (**“Full”** / **“Empty”**, **“Running”** / **“Stopped”**, **“Work”** / **“Transport”**) or its value (rpm, l/min) | The page of that device. [HUB-8 inputs](hub8-inputs.md) |

## Choose what a place shows

The strip has as many places as fit across the screen: 3 on an iPhone held upright, up to 8 on an iPad held sideways.

::: steps
1. Press and hold a tile for half a second. The list **“Choose value”** opens under it: every value the machine can show, with its icon and current value; the one in this place is marked.

2. Tap the value you want. If it is already in another place, the two swap.
:::

The choice is kept for the machine profile. **“Default slots”** in **“Settings”** › **“Machine”** puts speed, area, population and the first devices back.

## The alarm place

The place at the right is also the alarm place. When a device that is in no place of the strip goes into alarm, its tile stands there with a blinking ring until the alarm is over; a tap opens its page. While it is there, holding it opens no choice — the alarm is not hidden by a choice.

## The rate sheet

The rate sheet shows the rate in seeds per metre in large figures and the population in thousand seeds per hectare under it. Change it with **−** / **+** (hold for steps of ten), or tap a number and type it. Nothing reaches the gateway until you press **“Accept”**; swiping the sheet down leaves the rate as it was.

> **SEE ALSO**
>
> [The rows screen](rows-screen.md) · [Field](field-screen.md)


# The table

**“Table”** shows every row as a line of numbers. Use it when a bar tells you that something is wrong and you want the figures.

::: {.anatomy fig="app-table"}
1. **The page** — here **“Seed · k/ha”**. Tap the title to go to the next page.
2. **◄ ►** and the page number — go to the previous or the next page.
3. **“Reset”** — starts the counters of the table from zero. It asks first: **“Reset readings?”** — **“Yes”** or **“No”**.
4. **Column heads.** On this page: row number, **“s/m”** seeds per metre, **“Q.%”** quality, **“Db%”** doubles, **“Sk%”** skips, **“k/ha”** thousand seeds per hectare and **%** the deviation from the rate.
5. **A yellow cell** — the value is past half of its alarm level. Here row 3 has 14 % skips.
6. **A red cell** — the value is past its alarm level. Here row 5 has no flow: **-----** in place of the rate.
7. **The deviation from the rate**, red past the tolerance.
8. **Σ** — the summary line of all rows.

A planter in the Precision mode, on the test bench. The picture was taken earlier in the development; the top bar above the table is not shown.
:::

## The pages

What pages there are depends on the control mode of each group ([Products settings](settings-products.md)):

| Mode | Pages |
| --- | --- |
| Precision | Three seed pages: thousand seeds per hectare, seeds per metre, counters; then a fertilizer page if the fertilizer group is not in Precision |
| Hybrid | The counters page, in seeds per metre |
| Flow | The counters page, in seeds per second |

## Signs in the rate column

| Sign | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **-----** | No flow in the row |
| **!** | The row is taken off control |
| **X** | The sensor is not found |
| **?** | The device on the row's number is not a seed sensor |

Rows of the tramline are striped grey, as on the rows screen.

## What you can do

| To do this | Do this |
| --- | --- |
| Open the menu of a row | Tap its line. [The row menu](row-menu.md) |
| See more rows | Scroll the lines up or down. A sideways swipe turns the page of the app. |
| Start the counters from zero | **“Reset”** → **“Yes”** |

> **SEE ALSO**
>
> [Statistics](statistics-screen.md) · [The rows screen](rows-screen.md)


# Statistics

**“Statistics”** keeps the record of the work in five fields. One of them is active: everything the machine sows is counted into it.

::: {.anatomy fig="app-statistics"}
1. **The field on screen.** **(A)** marks the active field.
2. **◄ ►** and **1/5** — look at the other four fields.
3. **The menu …** — **“Select field”** and **“Reset statistics”**. [Below](#select-a-field-or-reset-it)
4. **“Field work”** — **“Distance”**, **“Area”**, **“Operating time”** and the average **“Ground speed”**.
5. When the work in this field **“Started”** and **“Ended”**.
6. **“Control”** — **“Without alarm control”** and **“Out of speed range”**. In this version both show a dash.
7. **The quality bar** of **“Seeding”**: **“Quality”**, **“Doubles”**, **“Skips”** and **“Not sown”** as shares of one bar (Precision).
8. **“Seeds sown”** (in thousands), **“Population”** and **“Rate”**: the actual value large, the set value under it, and the actual as a percentage of the set value — red past the tolerance.
9. **“Sown”**, **“Not sown”**, **“Unknown”** — in hectares when there is a speed; as shares of the time without one.
10. **The rows one by one** — the same figures for every sensor (**“Seed sensors”**, then the fertilizer sensors).

The statistics of a field on the test bench, after many hours of simulated work.
:::

What the **“Seeding”** block shows depends on the control mode of the group. In Precision you get the quality bar, the seeds sown, population and rate. In Flow and Hybrid you get the three amounts **“Sown”**, **“Not sown”** and **“Unknown”**. With two groups in Precision a page switch in the block's title shows the other group.

## Select a field or reset it

::: steps
1. Use **◄ ►** to bring the field you want onto the screen.

2. Tap **…** at the right of the title.

3. Choose:
   - **“Select field”** — this field becomes the active one. If it already holds statistics, the app first tells you **“Data must be erased to select this field!”**: **“Yes”** makes it active with its counters from zero.
   - **“Reset statistics”** — the app asks **“Are you sure?”**; **“Yes”** starts the statistics of this field from zero.
:::

**“Select field”** is offered only when the field on screen is not the active one.

> **IMPORTANT**
>
> **A reset cannot be undone.** The statistics of the field are gone. Changing the working width with statistics in the active field resets them too — the app asks first. See [Set up the machine profile](machine-profile.md).

> **SEE ALSO**
>
> [Table](table-screen.md) · [The tiles at the bottom](bottom-tiles.md)


# The field picture

**“Field”** draws the seeder as you would see it from the cab, standing on a field that moves under it. Every seed row is a column on the bar of the seeder — the same bar as on **“Rows”**, with its height and colour. Behind every row the ground is painted in the colour the row shows, and the painted strip runs away to the horizon at the speed of the machine. So you see the last metres of every row at a glance: a row that stopped leaves a gap that moves away from the seeder.

![The page “Field” from behind, with the tiles under it.](figures/app-field)

The picture is drawn from what the rows and the speed show at this moment. It is not a map: nothing is stored, and it has no GNSS track.

## What you can do

| To do this | Do this |
| --- | --- |
| Look from another side | Tap the picture. It turns through three views: from above, from behind, and from the front looking back (**“Looking back”** is written on it). The iPad keeps the last view. |
| See the fertilizer rows | With fertilizer sensors in the profile, switch between **“Seed”** and **“Fertilizer”** at the top. A red dot on the other choice tells you that a row of that group is red. |
| Use the tiles | The strip under the picture is the same as under **“Rows”**. [The tiles at the bottom](bottom-tiles.md) |

> **NOTE**
>
> **Without a speed the field still moves.** A Flow machine needs no speed, so the picture then moves at a fixed pace while seed flows. The distance in the picture is real only when there is a speed.

The alarms are not on this page: the alarm window opens over it as over every page. [The alarm window](alarm-window.md)


# The machine page

**“Machine”** shows everything on the seeder that is not a row: the devices on the HUB-8 hub, the rate, the tramline. On an iPad held sideways it has four blocks; on an iPhone and on an iPad held upright the blocks stand one under another.

::: {.anatomy fig="app-machine"}
1. **The page title.**
2. **“Devices”** — every device of the machine as a tile: its name, its state or value, and an icon in a ring coloured by its state. A fan and a metering unit turn while they work. Tap a tile to open the page of the device.
3. **“Motors · rate”** — the set rate of the seed group in Hybrid or Precision, large, with what it is under it. Tap the number to open the rate sheet.
4. **− / +** — change the rate by one step; hold for ten steps. Each step goes to the gateway at once.
5. **“Sections and tramline”** — the tramline bout, the rhythm and the actuators, when the machine has a tramline; a dash without one. [Tramline](tramline.md)
6. **“Device settings”** › **“Open in Settings”** — opens **“Settings”** › **“Machine”**.
7. **A device in alarm** — here the hopper is **“Empty”**: the ring is red and blinks.

The machine page of a bench machine with a fan, a metering unit, a hopper, the work position and a flowmeter.
:::

## When there is nothing to show

| The page says | Why | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **“The bridge is not connected”** | The app has no link to the gateway. | See [First connection to the gateway](first-connection.md). |
| **“No devices in the profile”** | The machine profile has no HUB-8 devices. | Add them: [HUB-8 inputs](hub8-inputs.md). |

The device states and their colours are the same as on the tiles of the rows screen. [The tiles at the bottom](bottom-tiles.md)

> **SEE ALSO**
>
> [HUB-8 inputs](hub8-inputs.md) · [Settings — Machine](settings-machine.md)


# The alarm window

An alarm is a window that opens over whatever page is on screen, with the buzzer. It tells you that a row, a device of the machine or the link to the gateway has a fault.

::: {.anatomy fig="app-alarm-window"}
1. **“ALARM!”** — the title strip of every alarm window; it blinks. Red for an alarm, orange for a device that reports itself faulty (**“Clogged”**, **“Light struck”**, **“Faulty”**, **“Wrong device type!”** …).
2. **The alarm** — here **“Hopper empty”**. Look it up by these words in the service codes.
3. **The sound line** — here **“Volume is off”**: the buzzer runs, but the tablet's volume is down. Turn it up.
4. **“Close”** — closes the window and stops the buzzer. The whole button takes the touch.
5. **The tile of the device in alarm**, with its ring blinking red.

An alarm of a HUB-8 device: the hopper is empty.
:::

For a row the window also names the sensor and the rows:

![The alarm window of four seed rows below the allowed rate.](figures/app-alarm-window-rows)

**“Seed sensor:”** or **“Fertilizer sensor:”** tells you which group, and the row numbers follow — **#4,12–14** means rows 4, 12, 13 and 14. For a tramline actuator the window says **“Tramline actuator”** and its number.

## How the window behaves

- **The fault must hold for the alarm delay** before the window opens — 3 seconds unless set otherwise in **“Settings”** › **“Control and Alarms”** › **“Alarm delay”** (2 to 20 seconds). A device that is not a seed sensor (**“Wrong device type!”**) is reported at once.
- **The same alarm in another row joins the open window**: its number is added. A different alarm waits until you close this one, then opens.
- **A closed alarm does not come back** while its fault lasts. It shows again only after the fault has gone and returned.
- **The link to the gateway comes first.** When the link has been down for 3 seconds, the window **“Bridge link lost”** replaces any other window: every figure on the screen is old. It closes by itself when the gateway answers again.
- **Closing the window does not repair the fault.** Active alarms stay in the list behind the bell — see [Moving around the app](app-navigation.md#the-list-of-alarms).

## The buzzer

The buzzer sounds while an alarm window is open: a short tone every two seconds, through the tablet's speaker. **“Close”** stops it. While a band is **“NOT UNDER CONTROL”** it sounds without a window.

In **“Settings”** › **“Control and Alarms”** › **“Alarm buzzer”**: **“Volume”** (**“Quiet”**, **“Medium”**, **“Loud”**), **“Test sound”**, and **“Quiet for 10 min”**. The silence mutes only the buzzer: the window still opens.

> **WARNING**
>
> **The tablet's own volume overrides the buzzer.** At zero volume the window opens in silence. Keep the volume up and watch for **“Volume is off”**.

> **SEE ALSO**
>
> [How service codes work](codes.md) · [Bar colours](bar-colours.md) · [Messages over the screen](screen-messages.md)


# Messages over the screen

Besides the alarm window, the app speaks through small capsules over the page. They are not windows: they need no closing and disappear when the cause is gone.

## Red capsule in the middle of the screen — the link to the gateway

While the red capsule is shown, the app has no live data: the page is dimmed and shows the last reading.

| The capsule says | What it means | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **“Looking for the bridge…”** | The app is looking for its gateway. | Check that the gateway has power and the tablet is close to it. |
| **“Connecting to”** and a name | The gateway is found; the app is connecting. | Wait. |
| **“Connection to”** a name **“lost, searching…”** | The link dropped; the app is looking for the same gateway again. | Wait; check the gateway's power. After 3 seconds the window **“Bridge link lost”** opens. [Code 601](codes-6-gateway-link.md#c601) |
| **“Bridge is silent…”** | The link is there, but the gateway sends nothing. | Wait 10 seconds; if it stays, switch the gateway's power off and on. [Code 602](codes-6-gateway-link.md#c602) |
| **“Choose bridge”** | Several gateways are in range, or yours is not found. Tap the capsule to open the list. | Tap your gateway. [First connection](first-connection.md) |
| **“Bluetooth is off”** | Bluetooth is off on the tablet. | Switch it on. [Code 704](codes-7-tablet.md#c704) |
| **“No Bluetooth permission”** | The app may not use Bluetooth. | Allow it in the iPad settings. [Code 705](codes-7-tablet.md#c705) |

## Yellow capsule at the top — the sound

| The capsule says | What it means | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **“Volume is off”** | The tablet's volume is below 20 %: an alarm would not be heard. | Turn the volume up. [Code 701](codes-7-tablet.md#c701) |
| **“Sound in headphones”** | The sound goes to headphones, a Bluetooth speaker or another device. | Disconnect it. [Code 702](codes-7-tablet.md#c702) |

The same yellow line appears inside the alarm window, so that you know why you did not hear it.

## Yellow capsule over a band — control

| The capsule says | What it means | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **“NOT UNDER CONTROL”** and the rows of the band, blinking | Seed flows in the band, but fewer of its rows sow within the norm than the set share. The buzzer sounds. | Check the control line or the rate and the yellow and dark-red rows. [Code 207](codes-2-seeding.md#c207) |

> **SEE ALSO**
>
> [The alarm window](alarm-window.md) · [What you need](what-you-need.md)


# Settings

Open the settings with the gear at the right of the top bar, or with **“Settings”** on the tab bar of an iPhone. On an iPad the groups stand in a list at the left and the open group at the right; on an iPhone a group opens over the list. A change takes effect at once — there is no Save button.

::: {.anatomy fig="app-settings"}
1. **“Products”** — what we sow: the control mode, the fraction, the rate. [Products](settings-products.md)
2. **“Control and Alarms”** — how the rows are judged: the share of seeding rows, the alarm delay, the tolerance, the buzzer. [Control and Alarms](settings-control-alarms.md)
3. **“Machine”** — the machine profile, the devices, the tramline and the gateway. It is open here. [Machine](settings-machine.md)
4. **“App”** — language, sound of the buttons, screen, home page, help and version. [App](settings-app.md)
5. **“Service”** — locked, for the Agriwelt service.
6. **“Machine profile”** — the rows and the fertilizer sensors. [Set up the machine profile](machine-profile.md)
7. **The profile status line** — what the gateway answered, here **“profile read from the bridge at”** and the time.
8. **“Number the sensors”** — [Number the sensors](sensor-numbering.md)
9. **HUB-8** — the devices of the machine. [HUB-8 inputs](hub8-inputs.md)

The settings of the group **“Machine”** on an iPad.
:::

The settings that the gateway must know — the profile, the fraction, the rate — are sent to it by the app. While the link to the gateway is down, the control mode, the fraction and the rate are greyed out, and the sensors cannot be numbered.

> **SEE ALSO**
>
> [Moving around the app](app-navigation.md) · [The built-in help](built-in-help.md)


# Settings — Products: control mode, fraction and rate

**“Settings”** › **“Products”** has a section **“Seed”** and, with fertilizer sensors in the profile, a section **“Fertilizer”**. Each group has its own settings.

## Control mode

**“Control mode”** decides how the rows of the group are judged.

| Mode | What it measures | What it needs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Flow | Seeds per second in every row, against the control line you drag on the rows screen. A row below the line is yellow; a row without flow is red. | Nothing more: no speed, no area. |
| **“Hybrid”** | Seeds per metre of row, in whole numbers, from the iPad's GNSS speed. A row below the tolerance band shows **“Under allowable rate”**, above it **“Rate too high”**. Doubles and skips are not counted. | An iPad with GNSS and Location allowed. |
| **“Precision”** | Seeds per metre with tenths, from the GNSS speed. The sensors also count doubles and skips. Without a fresh speed for 2 seconds the row menu says **“Unknown: no speed”**. | An iPad with GNSS and Location allowed. |

Hybrid and Precision are offered only when the iPad gives a speed. The first time you pick one, the app shows **“Waiting for the iPad's GNSS speed…”**; if no speed comes, only Flow stays. See [What you need](what-you-need.md).

## Rate (Hybrid and Precision)

**“Rate”** — the seeds per metre you want, with **−** / **+**. Under it **“Thousand seeds/ha”** — the same rate per hectare, worked out from the working width — and the alarm band: the rate below and above which a row raises an alarm, from **“Rate tolerance”** in [Control and Alarms](settings-control-alarms.md).

You can also change the rate on the rows screen (drag the rate column), on the **“Population”** or **“Rate”** tile, and on the page **“Machine”**.

## Fraction

**“Fraction”** — the setting of the sensors for the size of the seed. Pick the crop or the seed size: **“Rapeseed”**, **“Wheat”**, **“Barley”**, **“Soybean”**, **“Peas”**, **“Beans”**, **“Maize”**, **“Sunflower”**, **“Small”**, **“Medium”**, **“Large”** or **“Pneumatic drill”**. The number in brackets is what the sensor receives.

There is one fraction for all seed rows and one for all fertilizer rows. The gateway sends it to every sensor of the group; the rows then show the setup bar one after another, a few seconds each.

**“Expert”** opens **“Value for the sensor”**, the number itself, for the service.

## Max seeding in tramline

**“Max seeding in tramline,%”** — shown on machines with a tramline. A row in the tramline that sows more than this share of the rate raises **“Seeding in tramline”**. From 0 to 50 %, 20 % unless changed. See [Tramline](tramline.md).

> **SEE ALSO**
>
> [Control and Alarms settings](settings-control-alarms.md) · [The rows screen](rows-screen.md)


# Settings — Control and Alarms

**“Settings”** › **“Control and Alarms”** decides how the rows are judged and how loud the alarm is.

## Flow control

| Setting | What it does | Range | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **“Share of seeding rows”** | Control starts when at least this share of the rows sows within the norm for 3 seconds running, and stops at once when the share is lost. While it is under control, the machine counts as seeding. | 5–80 %, steps of 5 | 20 % |
| **“Alarm delay”** | How long a fault of a row must hold before the alarm window opens. | 2–20 s | 3 s |
| **“Separate share for fertilizer”** | With fertilizer sensors: gives the fertilizer band a share of its own, **“Share of seeding fertilizer rows”**. Off — it uses the seed share. | — | Off |

The machine counts as seeding when at least one band — seed or fertilizer — is under control.

> **TIP**
>
> **If the app alarms too often on a rough field, raise “Alarm delay” first.** A short delay reacts to every bump; a long one lets a real fault run longer before you hear it.

## Hybrid and precision seeding

Shown when a group is in Hybrid or Precision. One value for the whole machine.

| Setting | What it does | Range | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **“Rate tolerance”** | The band around the rate: below it **“Under allowable rate”**, above it **“Rate too high”**. | 5–95 %, steps of 5 | 50 % |
| **“Doubles alarm level”** | Share of doubles in the last 20 m above which **“Too many doubles”** is raised. **“No”** — no alarm. | No, 1–95 % | No |
| **“Skips alarm level”** | The same for skips: **“Too many skips”**. | No, 1–95 % | No |
| **“Skips & doubles”** | Narrow bars beside each row's column: skips at the left, doubles at the right. The figures are always in the table. | On / Off | Off |

## Alarm buzzer

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **“Volume”** | **“Quiet”**, **“Medium”** or **“Loud”** (default). The tablet's own volume still limits it. |
| **“Test sound”** | Plays one beep at the chosen volume. |
| **“Quiet for 10 min”** | Mutes the buzzer for 10 minutes. **“Silence”** shows the minutes left; **“Cancel silence”** ends it. |

> **IMPORTANT**
>
> **“Quiet for 10 min” mutes the buzzer, not the alarm.** The alarm window always opens; only the sound is held back for those ten minutes.

> **SEE ALSO**
>
> [The alarm window](alarm-window.md) · [Products settings](settings-products.md)


# Settings — Machine

**“Settings”** › **“Machine”** holds everything the app and the gateway need to know about the seeder. The page **“Machine”** of the ring leads here with **“Open in Settings”**.

| Section | What is in it | Where it is explained |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **“Machine profile”** | **“Rows”**, **“Fertilizer sensors”**, **“Sensors on the bus now”**, the status line of the profile in the gateway; in Hybrid and Precision **“Width, cm”** and **“Row spacing”**; the button **“Number the sensors”**. | [Set up the machine profile](machine-profile.md) · [Number the sensors](sensor-numbering.md) |
| **“Devices”** | **HUB-8** — the devices of the machine and the inputs they take; **“Default slots”** — puts the default values back into the tiles at the bottom. | [HUB-8 inputs](hub8-inputs.md) · [The tiles at the bottom](bottom-tiles.md) |
| **“Tramline”** | The number of tramline actuators, the switch **“Tramline”**, the rhythm, the mapping of actuators to rows and every actuator. Shown only on machines that can have a tramline. | [Tramline](tramline.md) |
| **“Bridge”** | The link and its signal, **“My bridge”**, **“Reconnect”**, **“Forget bridge”**, **“Bridge firmware”**, **“Hardware revision”**, **“Bridge update”** and the link counters; in Hybrid and Precision also **“GNSS speed”** with its age in seconds. | [First connection to the gateway](first-connection.md) · [Update the gateway](bridge-update.md) |

## The profile status line

Under the numbers of the profile a line says what the gateway did with it:

| The line says | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **“profile read from the bridge at”** and a time | The app read the profile from the gateway on connecting. |
| **“writing the profile to the bridge…”** | A change is on its way. |
| **“profile written to the bridge at”** and a time | The gateway took the change. |
| **“profile not yet read from the bridge”** | Nothing has been read since the app started. |
| A message with a code | The gateway refused. See [9xx · Setup answers of the gateway](codes-9-setup.md). |

## GNSS speed

**“GNSS speed”** shows the speed the iPad gives and how many seconds old it is, for example “10.0 km/h · 0 s”. When there is no fresh speed it shows **“no speed”** in orange. [Code 703](codes-7-tablet.md#c703)

> **SEE ALSO**
>
> [Settings](settings.md) · [The machine page](machine-screen.md)


# Settings — App

**“Settings”** › **“App”** holds the settings of the app itself. They are kept on the tablet, not in the gateway.

| Section | Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **“Language and appearance”** | **“Language”** | **“System”** (the tablet's language), Ukrainian, German or English. The app changes language at once. |
| | **“Theme”** | **“Dark · for the cab”** — the only theme. |
| **“Sound”** | **“Buttons sound”** | A click on every button. Off unless switched on. |
| **“Work screen”** | **“Keep screen awake”** | The tablet does not dim or lock its screen while the app is open. |
| — | **“Home screen of the Seeding tab”** | What **“Home”** and the start of the app open: **“Rows”**, or **“Last opened”** — the page of the ring you were on last, also after a restart. |
| — | **“Help”** | The built-in help. [The built-in help](built-in-help.md) |
| **“About”** | **“Version”** | The version of the app. Give it to the service with the gateway's firmware version. |

> **TIP**
>
> **Keep the screen on in the cab** — with **“Keep screen awake”**, or with the tablet's own Auto-Lock set to Never. A screen that goes dark hides the alarm window.

> **SEE ALSO**
>
> [What you need](what-you-need.md) · [Settings](settings.md)


# Number the sensors

Every sensor on the sensor line answers on its own number, and the app knows a row by that number. A new sensor must get the number of its row before it is watched. The app does this through the gateway, from one sheet with two doors:

- **“Settings”** › **“Machine”** › **“Number the sensors”** — for commissioning;
- the row menu › **“Replace the sensor”** — for one row in the field; the row's number is already set.

The sheet has the list **“On the bus”** on top. At the bottom stays a panel that does not scroll: **“Sensor”**, **“New number”** and the button **“Assign No.”**. **“Close”** is in the header.

> **IMPORTANT**
>
> **While the sheet is open, the gateway does not watch the rows.** No row alarm comes during numbering. Do it with the machine standing, and close the sheet when you are done.

## Replace a sensor in the field

::: steps
1. Stop the machine. Connect the new sensor in place of the old one; the old one must be off the line, because the button stays off while it still answers on this number.

2. Open the row menu of the row (press and hold its bar) and tap **“Replace the sensor”**. The sheet **“Replace the sensor”** opens: the new sensor gets this row's number; the machine profile does not change.

3. Under **“On the bus”** the app lists the sensors that answer, each with its number and its place: **“row 5”**, **“fertiliser, row 5”** or **“outside the profile”**. Sensors outside the profile come first. Before the first answer the list says **“searching…”**; with no sensor on the line it says **“No sensor on the bus.”** If it is the only one, the app chooses it by itself: **“The only sensor outside the profile — chosen by itself.”** Otherwise tap the new sensor in the list.

4. Check **“New number”** — it is the row's number — and tap **“Assign No.”** with the number.

5. The sheet shows the steps: **“sending the command to the bridge…”**, **“sensor found”**, **“number written”**, **“saved for good”**, **“rebooting, waiting for the answer…”**, **“answers on the new number”**. It is done only when the sensor answers on its new number: **“Done.”** with the old and the new number and **“sensor answers”**.

6. Tap **“Close”**.
:::

## Commission a seeder

Open **“Number the sensors”** and number the sensors one by one: pick a sensor in the list **“On the bus”**, set **“New number”**, tap **“Assign No.”**. The number can be any from 1 to 199; set it with the minus and plus keys. The app first offers the first free row of the profile, or, when all rows are taken, the number after the last row. Under the number the hint names the place of that number: **“row 5”**, **“fertiliser, row 5”** or **“outside the profile (rows: 24)”**. Sensors can be numbered on the full sensor line, as long as each has a number of its own.

> **NOTE**
>
> **Connect new sensors one at a time.** When two sensors answer on the same number, the gateway cannot tell them apart and stops with **“More than one device on the network!”**.

## When it does not work

| The sheet says | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| **“Address taken”** (the button stays off) | Another sensor already answers on this number. Choose a free number, or first renumber the sensor that holds it. [Code 920](codes-9-setup.md#c920) |
| **“The sensor already has this number”** | Nothing to do. |
| **“Number outside 1…199”** | Set a number from 1 to 199. [Code 916](codes-9-setup.md#c916) |
| **“Pick the sensor in the list “On the bus””** | Tap a sensor in the list. |
| **“Address 7 already used!”** (with the number you chose) | The gateway found that number taken. Choose a free number. [Code 920](codes-9-setup.md#c920) |
| **“No connection”** and **“at step:”** … | The sensor stopped answering at that step: **“finding the sensor”**, **“writing the number”**, **“saving”**, **“restart”** or **“check on the new number”**. Check its plug and the power of the sensor line, and try again. [Code 913](codes-9-setup.md#c913) |
| **“More than one device on the network!”** | Leave only one new sensor connected. [Code 914](codes-9-setup.md#c914) |
| **“Bridge busy: seed is still flowing. Stop the seeder and retry in a minute.”** | Stop the seeder and wait a minute. [Code 912](codes-9-setup.md#c912) |
| **“The bridge did not answer”** | The gateway sent no answer for 30 seconds. Check the link to the gateway and try again. |
| **“Seed is still flowing — the bridge does not listen to the bus. Stop the seeder.”** | Stop the seeder. [Code 912](codes-9-setup.md#c912) |
| **“The bridge is busy with another action, please wait.”** | Wait and try again. [Code 917](codes-9-setup.md#c917) |
| **“Error #”** and a number | See [9xx · Setup answers of the gateway](codes-9-setup.md). |

**“Number the sensors”** and **“Replace the sensor”** are greyed out while the link to the gateway is down.


# Tramline

The app counts the bouts of the tramline rhythm. On the bouts of the rhythm the rows of the tramline actuators go quiet: their columns are hatched grey, they raise no **“Not seeding”**, and a row that sows anyway raises **“Seeding in tramline”**.

## Settings

**“Settings”** › **“Machine”**, section **“Tramline”** — shown only on machines that can have a tramline.

![The tramline section of the machine settings.](figures/app-tramline-settings)

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **“Tramline actuators”** | How many tramline actuators the machine has. |
| **“Tramline”** | Switches the tramline on or off. |
| **“Tramline rhythm settings”** | The rhythm: choose one of three rhythms with **“Select”** — the active one is marked **“Active”** —, set its number of **“Bouts”** (1–50), and under **“Tramline actuators activation”** the bouts on which each actuator shuts its rows (up to four per actuator). **“Reset rhythm settings”** clears the rhythm. |
| **“Actuators to sensors mapping”** | Which rows each actuator shuts — up to four ranges of rows per actuator. |
| **“Tramline actuator”** #1, #2 … | Every actuator: its state, **“Cutoff position”** (**“Extended”** or **“Retracted”**), **“Switch”** (**“when seeding”** or **“always”**), and **“Disable control”** / **“Enable control”**. |
| **“Auto switching source”** | The first choice in the list — the bout changes by itself: by the markers when the machine has them, otherwise on every lift of the seeder. |

An actuator taken off control is virtual: its rows go quiet by the rhythm, but the gateway does not drive it.

In **“Settings”** › **“Products”**, **“Max seeding in tramline,%”** sets how much a tramline row may sow before **“Seeding in tramline”** (20 % of the rate unless changed). [Products settings](settings-products.md)

## The bout tile and the bout menu

On the rows screen the tile **“Bout”** shows the current bout over the bouts of the rhythm, for example “2 / 4”, and the rhythm. Its ring is green while the bout changes by itself and yellow while it does not; it turns red and blinks when an actuator is in alarm.

Tap the tile to open the menu **“Tramline”**:

![The bout menu over the rows screen.](figures/app-tramline-bout-menu)

| Item | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **“Next bout”** | Moves to the next bout and closes the menu. Offered when the bout cannot change by itself. |
| **“Auto switching”** | Switches the automatic change of the bout on or off. Offered when the machine can change it by itself. |
| **“Active bout”** | Sets the bout with **−** / **+**. Written when the menu closes. |

**“Done”** closes the menu.

> **SEE ALSO**
>
> [4xx · Tramline actuators](codes-4-tramline.md) · [Code 206](codes-2-seeding.md#c206) · [Bar colours](bar-colours.md)


# HUB-8 inputs — the devices of the machine

The HUB-8 hub brings the other devices of the machine onto the sensor line. The gateway only reads its inputs; what is wired to an input — a hopper sensor, a fan sensor, the work position — is known only to the app. So you tell the app what is on the machine, and the app works out which input each device takes.

Open **“Settings”** › **“Machine”** › **HUB-8**. The page **“Devices”** opens.

## Devices on the machine

Under **“Devices on the machine”** set how many of each kind the machine has, with **−** / **+**. The limits: 2 fans, 9 metering units, 9 hoppers, one of every other kind; metering units, hoppers and tractor inputs together at most 12. At a limit the **+** stays off.

## Which input each device takes

The devices take the inputs of the HUB-8 in a fixed order: speed sensor → fans → metering units → hoppers → tractor inputs → work position → flowmeter. The first device in this order is wired to input 1, the next to input 2, and so on. The list **“HUB-8 inputs”** shows every input with its device and its live state.

> **IMPORTANT**
>
> **Adding a device moves the devices after it.** Add a hopper, and the work position moves one input further. Rewire the HUB-8 to the new list. If the gateway holds the devices in another order, the page says **“Addresses in the bridge do not follow the ribbon”**; tap **“Lay out by the ribbon”**.

The markers are not on the HUB-8: they are wired to the tramline controller. Switch them on in the section of the markers at the bottom of the page.

The section **“Profile in the bridge”** shows whether the gateway has taken the list.

## The settings of each device

Tap a device in the list (or its tile on the rows screen) to open its page: its state and its **“Parameters”**.

| Device | Parameters | When it alarms |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **“Work position”** | **“Transport position signal”** (0 or 1), **“Alarm criterion”** | The state is shown as **“Work”** or **“Transport”**. In transport position — the seeder lifted out of work, on the headland turn too — **“Under allowable rate”**, **“Not seeding”**, a slow fan and a stopped metering unit stay silent. Seed sensor faults sound in transport position too. |
| **“Hopper”** | **“Signal “empty””** is 1 | Always, even with the machine standing: **“Hopper empty”**. |
| **“Fan”** | **“Pulses per revolution”** (1–60), **“Min, rpm”** and **“Max, rpm”** (500–9000) | Too fast — always; too slow — only while seeding. |
| **“Metering unit”** | **“Period, s”** (1–60) | Not turning for longer than the period while seeding: **“Dispenser not turning”**. |
| **“Oil pressure”**, **“Battery charge”** | **“Alarm signal”** (0 or 1), **“Delay, s”** (1–30) | The signal must hold for the delay. With an ignition input, only with the ignition on. |
| **“Fuel”**, **“Air filter”** | **“Alarm signal”**, **“Delay, s”** | The signal must hold for the delay. |
| **“Ignition”** | **“Signal “on””** | Never — it is a state that the oil pressure and battery charge depend on. |
| **“Flowmeter”** | **“Pulses per litre”** (1–60000) | — It shows litres per minute and the litres so far. |
| **“Left marker”**, **“Right marker”** | **“Signal “lowered””** | — They are shown as **“Lowered”** or **“Raised”**. |

The states shown in the list and on the tiles: **“no data”** — nothing read yet; **“silent”** — the input does not answer; **“wrong device”** — another kind of device answers. The alarms of these devices: [3xx · Hopper, fan, metering unit and tractor inputs](codes-3-machine-devices.md).

> **SEE ALSO**
>
> [The machine page](machine-screen.md) · [The tiles at the bottom](bottom-tiles.md)


# Update the gateway

The Hectare app carries the firmware for the gateway. When the app holds a newer version than the gateway runs, it offers the update. The update goes over Bluetooth and takes about 3 minutes. The gateway writes the new firmware into a spare part of its memory; the working firmware stays untouched and keeps working until the new one has proved itself. Your machine settings (the row profile) are not erased by the update.

Open **“Settings”** › **“Machine”** › **“Bridge”** › **“Bridge update”**. The row **“Bridge update”** shows at its right the version the app can install; empty means there is nothing to install. The page shows **“Version in the bridge”** and **“Version in the app”**.

| The page says | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **“Update the bridge to”** and a version | An update is offered. |
| **“The bridge has the newest version”** | Nothing to do. |
| **“The bridge is not connected”** | Connect first: [First connection to the gateway](first-connection.md). |
| **“The bridge cannot be updated over Bluetooth”** | This gateway cannot take an update from the app. Ask Agriwelt. |

The app offers only firmware made for this gateway board, and only a version newer than the one the gateway runs. Anything else is not offered at all.

## Run the update

::: steps
1. Stop the machine. Keep the gateway powered and your device — tablet or phone — close to it.

2. Tap **“Update the bridge to”**. The conditions appear under **“Before the update”**: **“The bridge is powered, the device is near it.”** · **“The machine stands: do not seed during the update.”** · **“Takes about 3 minutes.”** · **“Do not leave the app or lock the screen.”**

3. Tap **“Start the update”** (or **“Cancel”**). Three stages follow: **“Firmware transfer”** with a percentage, **“Bridge restart”**, **“Checking the new firmware”**. Do not leave the app and do not walk away with the device. The screen does not dim and the back button is hidden until the result appears.

4. The result appears with its code, for example **“804 · Bridge updated”**. Tap **“Done”**.
:::

The whole update takes 2 to 2.5 minutes: the transfer 1 to 1.5 minutes (57 seconds on an iPhone XS, 95 seconds on an iPad), the restart 12 to 25 seconds, the check about 25 seconds.

## After the restart {#after-the-restart}

About 20 seconds after the new firmware starts, the gateway checks itself — its radio, the sensor line, its settings and its device description — and keeps the new firmware only if everything is in order. If the check fails, the app restarts the gateway once more after 50 seconds and it returns to the previous firmware (code 805); this takes about 2.5 minutes. If no device with the app is near at that moment, the gateway keeps working on the unconfirmed firmware until it is switched off and on, and then returns to the previous one by itself.

During the update the rows are not watched: the app raises no **“Bridge link lost”** and the buzzer is silent.

## The results

| Result | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| **804 · “Bridge updated”** | Nothing. The gateway runs the new firmware and works as before. |
| **805 · “The bridge went back to its previous firmware”** | The new firmware failed its check; the gateway runs the previous one and works. Tell the service the code. |
| **806 · “The bridge refused the firmware: the signature does not match”** | Update the app and try again. If it repeats, tell the service the code. |
| **807 · “The bridge refused the firmware: it is not newer”** | Nothing. The gateway keeps its own firmware. |
| **808 · “Firmware transfer interrupted”** | Keep the device near the gateway and try again; the transfer starts over. |
| **809 · “The bridge is busy: no update now”** or **“The machine is seeding: the update did not start”** | Finish seeding, clear the active alarm, wait a minute and try again. |
| **810 · “The bridge did not come back after the restart”** | Check the gateway's power, wait a minute. Not back — switch its power off and on and open this page again. |

Every result: [8xx · Gateway update](codes-8-gateway-update.md).

> **WARNING**
>
> **Do not switch the gateway off during the update.** If the transfer breaks off, the gateway stays on its previous firmware; start again.


# The help inside the app

The app carries five short help topics that work without a network. Open **“Settings”** › **“App”** › **“Help”**, then tap a topic; **‹** goes back to the list.

| Topic in the app | What it explains | More in this help |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **“Bar colours and the three reds”** | What the colours of a row's bar mean, and the three different reds. | [Bar colours](bar-colours.md) |
| **“The line, by finger”** | How to move the control line by pressing and dragging the rate column. | [The rows screen](rows-screen.md) |
| **“Disable control”** | How to open the row menu and take a row off control, and how to put it back. | [The row menu](row-menu.md) |
| **“Alarm window”** | What the alarm window shows, how rows join it, and where the volume is set. | [The alarm window](alarm-window.md) |
| **“Bridge”** | What the gateway is, where its state is shown, and how to pick your gateway from the list. | [First connection to the gateway](first-connection.md) |

The help is reached only from the settings; the alarm window has no link to it. The service codes are not in the app's help; they are here: [How service codes work](codes.md).


# How service codes work

Every alarm, fault and notable event of an Agrigate system has a service code of three digits. A code never changes its meaning: if you tell the service “102 on row 7”, they know what happened without seeing the screen.

## The three digits

The first digit is the part of the system; the other two are the kind of fault.

| Code | Part of the system |
| --- | --- |
| [1xx](codes-1-row-sensor.md) | The sensor of a row itself |
| [2xx](codes-2-seeding.md) | The seeding of a row — the sensor works, the row sows wrong |
| [3xx](codes-3-machine-devices.md) | The devices on the HUB-8: hopper, fan, metering unit, tractor inputs |
| [4xx](codes-4-tramline.md) | Tramline actuators |
| 5xx | Not used in this version |
| [6xx](codes-6-gateway-link.md) | The gateway and the link to it |
| [7xx](codes-7-tablet.md) | The iPad or iPhone |
| [8xx](codes-8-gateway-update.md) | Updating the gateway |
| [9xx](codes-9-setup.md) | The gateway's answers when the app sets something up |

## The place is shown beside the code

The code says *what*; the place says *where*. It is written beside the code, not in it: “102 · row 7”, “301 · hopper”, “404 · tramline actuator #2”. So the same code covers every row and every device.

## The four classes {#classes}

### Alarm {#class-alarm}

A window with a red title strip **“ALARM!”** and the buzzer. Something on the machine needs you now. [The alarm window](alarm-window.md)

### Device fault {#class-fault}

The same window with an orange title strip, and the buzzer. A device reports that it is faulty — clogged, light struck, the wrong kind of device.

### Attention {#class-attention}

No window. A yellow capsule or a line next to what you are doing — for example **“Volume is off”**, or a message on the setup page. Read it and act when you can. [Messages over the screen](screen-messages.md)

### Record {#class-record}

Nothing to do. The event is kept for the service.

## Finding a code from the screen

> **NOTE**
>
> **In this pre-release version the alarm window shows the words of the alarm, not its code.** Find the words in the code topics — every code there gives the words the app shows. The update of the gateway shows its codes on screen, for example **“804 · Bridge updated”**. For the setup answers of the gateway the app shows a number after the words; see [9xx](codes-9-setup.md).

Two codes share their words on screen: 201 and 202 both say **“Under allowable rate”**. The bar tells them apart — yellow for 201, dark red blinking for 202 — and so does the row menu (**“Not seeding”** for 202).

## When you call the service

Give the code (or the words on the screen), the place — the row or the device —, and from **“Settings”**: the version of the app (**“App”** › **“Version”**) and the firmware of the gateway (**“Machine”** › **“Bridge firmware”**).


# 1xx · Row sensor faults

Codes 1xx belong to the sensor of a row itself: the sensor does not answer, or it reports that it cannot count. The place is the row: tell the service, for example, “102 · row 7”. The window title is orange for a device fault and red for an alarm.

How to read a code, the four classes and how each looks in the app: [How service codes work](codes.md).

## 101 · Row sensor not answering {#c101}

**Class:** [Alarm](codes.md#class-alarm) · **Place:** the row.

**What you see.** The alarm window with **“Connection lost”**, **“Seed sensor:”** or **“Fertilizer sensor:”** and the row numbers. The bar of the row shows a red ✕ on a grey background. When several rows lose the link, their numbers join one window.

**What to do:**

1. Check the plug and the cable of the sensor of this row.
2. If several rows next to each other are silent, look for a broken main cable or lost power before the first of them.
3. If only this row is silent and its cable is good, replace the sensor: [Number the sensors](sensor-numbering.md).

## 102 · Row sensor clogged {#c102}

**Class:** [Device fault](codes.md#class-fault) · **Place:** the row.

**What you see.** The alarm window with an orange title, **“Clogged”** and the row number. The bar of the row keeps showing its level.

**What to do:**

1. Stop.
2. Clean the seed tube and the window of the sensor of this row.

## 103 · Row sensor light struck {#c103}

**Class:** [Device fault](codes.md#class-fault) · **Place:** the row.

**What you see.** The alarm window with an orange title, **“Light struck”** and the row number.

**What to do:**

1. Shade the sensor from direct light: check its cover and the position of the seed tube.
2. If it comes back in the shade too, tell the service the code and the row number.

## 104 · Row sensor faulty {#c104}

**Class:** [Device fault](codes.md#class-fault) · **Place:** the row.

**What you see.** The alarm window with an orange title, **“Faulty”** and the row number.

**What to do:**

1. Unplug the sensor and plug it in again.
2. If the fault stays, replace the sensor (row menu, **“Replace the sensor”**). Until then you can take the row off control: **“Disable control”** in the row menu.

## 105 · Row sensor reports another fault {#c105}

**Class:** [Device fault](codes.md#class-fault) · **Place:** the row.

**What you see.** The alarm window with an orange title, **“Other fault”** and the row number.

**What to do:**

1. Tell the service the code and the row number.
2. You can take the row off control (**“Disable control”** in the row menu) and go on seeding.

## 106 · Not a seed sensor on this row {#c106}

**Class:** [Device fault](codes.md#class-fault) · **Place:** the row.

**What you see.** The alarm window with an orange title, **“Wrong device type!”** and the row number. The bar blinks bright red with a “?”. This alarm comes at once, without the alarm delay.

**What to do:**

1. Check that a seed sensor, not another device, is connected for this row.
2. Correct the numbering: [Number the sensors](sensor-numbering.md).


# 2xx · Seeding alarms

Codes 2xx mean that the sensor of the row works and the seeding itself is wrong: the cause is on the seeder, not in the electronics. The place is the row.

How to read a code, the four classes and how each looks in the app: [How service codes work](codes.md).

## 201 · Row below the allowed rate {#c201}

**Class:** [Alarm](codes.md#class-alarm) · **Place:** the row.

**What you see.** The alarm window with **“Under allowable rate”** and the row numbers. The bar of the row is yellow: below the control line (Flow) or below the tolerance band (Hybrid, Precision).

**What to do:**

1. Check the metering unit and the seed tube of this row.
2. Check that there is seed above the metering unit.

## 202 · Row not seeding {#c202}

**Class:** [Alarm](codes.md#class-alarm) · **Place:** the row.

**What you see.** The alarm window with **“Under allowable rate”** and the row numbers — the same words as code 201. The column of the row blinks dark red; the row menu says **“Not seeding”**. The sensor answers, no seed passes it, while most rows sow.

**What to do:**

1. Stop: the row does not sow.
2. Check the metering unit, its drive and the seed tube of this row.
3. Check that there is seed in the hopper.

## 203 · Row above the allowed rate {#c203}

**Class:** [Alarm](codes.md#class-alarm) · **Place:** the row.

**What you see.** The alarm window with **“Rate too high”** and the row numbers. The bar of the row is blue. Only in the Hybrid and Precision modes.

**What to do:**

1. Check the setting of the metering unit of this row.

## 204 · Too many doubles {#c204}

**Class:** [Alarm](codes.md#class-alarm) · **Place:** the row.

**What you see.** The alarm window with **“Too many doubles”** and the row numbers. Only in the Precision mode, and only when **“Doubles alarm level”** is not set to **“No”**.

**What to do:**

1. Check the seed disc, the doubles eliminator and the vacuum of this row.

## 205 · Too many skips {#c205}

**Class:** [Alarm](codes.md#class-alarm) · **Place:** the row.

**What you see.** The alarm window with **“Too many skips”** and the row numbers. Only in the Precision mode, and only when **“Skips alarm level”** is not set to **“No”**.

**What to do:**

1. Check the seed disc and the vacuum of this row.
2. Check the ground speed: drive slower if it is too high for the disc.

## 206 · Seeding into the tramline {#c206}

**Class:** [Alarm](codes.md#class-alarm) · **Place:** the row.

**What you see.** The alarm window with **“Seeding in tramline”** and the row numbers. The column of the row is hatched grey (tramline) and the seed over it is hatched red.

**What to do:**

1. Check the shutter or the clutch of the tramline on this row.
2. If the row should sow, check the tramline rhythm and the actuator settings: [Tramline](tramline.md).

## 207 · Seeding without control {#c207}

**Class:** [Attention](codes.md#class-attention) · **Place:** the row.

**What you see.** No window. The yellow capsule **“NOT UNDER CONTROL”** with the rows of the band blinks over the band, and the buzzer sounds. Seed flows in the band, but fewer of its rows sow within the norm than **“Share of seeding rows”** asks for — for example when the control line or the rate is far from what the rows really sow.

**What to do:**

1. Check the control line or the rate against what the rows really sow.
2. Check the rows that are yellow or dark red: [Bar colours](bar-colours.md).


# 3xx · Hopper, fan, metering unit and tractor inputs
