Codes 3xx come from the devices wired to the HUB-8 hub: hopper level, fan speed, metering unit rotation and the tractor inputs (oil pressure, battery charge, fuel, air filter). The place is the device, for example “301 · hopper”. How the devices are set up: [HUB-8 inputs](hub8-inputs.md).

How to read a code, the four classes and how each looks in the app: [How service codes work](codes.md).

## 301 · Hopper empty {#c301}

**Class:** [Alarm](codes.md#class-alarm) · **Place:** the device.

**What you see.** The alarm window with **“Hopper empty”**. The hopper tile shows **“Empty”** with a red ring. This alarm sounds even when the machine stands.

**What to do:**

1. Fill the hopper.
2. If the hopper is full, check the level sensor and its setting: [HUB-8 inputs](hub8-inputs.md).

## 302 · Fan too slow {#c302}

**Class:** [Alarm](codes.md#class-alarm) · **Place:** the device.

**What you see.** The alarm window with **“Fan speed too low”**. The fan tile shows the speed in rpm with a red ring. Only while seeding.

**What to do:**

1. Raise the fan speed: hydraulic flow, engine speed.
2. Check **“Min, rpm”** and **“Pulses per revolution”** of the fan: [HUB-8 inputs](hub8-inputs.md).

## 303 · Fan too fast {#c303}

**Class:** [Alarm](codes.md#class-alarm) · **Place:** the device.

**What you see.** The alarm window with **“Fan speed too high”**. The fan tile shows the speed in rpm with a red ring.

**What to do:**

1. Lower the fan speed.
2. Check **“Max, rpm”** and **“Pulses per revolution”** of the fan: [HUB-8 inputs](hub8-inputs.md).

## 304 · Metering unit not turning {#c304}

**Class:** [Alarm](codes.md#class-alarm) · **Place:** the device.

**What you see.** The alarm window with **“Dispenser not turning”**. The metering unit tile shows **“Stopped”** with a red ring. Only while seeding, after the time set in **“Period, s”**.

**What to do:**

1. Stop: the metering unit does not turn.
2. Check its drive, the chain and the clutch.
3. If it does turn, check the shaft sensor and **“Period, s”**.

## 305 · Oil pressure low {#c305}

**Class:** [Alarm](codes.md#class-alarm) · **Place:** the device.

**What you see.** The alarm window with **“Emergency oil pressure”**. With an ignition input it sounds only with the ignition on.

**What to do:**

1. Stop the engine.
2. Check the oil level.

## 306 · Battery not charging {#c306}

**Class:** [Alarm](codes.md#class-alarm) · **Place:** the device.

**What you see.** The alarm window with **“No battery charge”**. With an ignition input it sounds only with the ignition on.

**What to do:**

1. Check the alternator and its belt.

## 307 · Fuel low {#c307}

**Class:** [Alarm](codes.md#class-alarm) · **Place:** the device.

**What you see.** The alarm window with **“Low fuel”**.

**What to do:**

1. Refuel.

## 308 · Air filter clogged {#c308}

**Class:** [Alarm](codes.md#class-alarm) · **Place:** the device.

**What you see.** The alarm window with **“Air filter clogged”**.

**What to do:**

1. Clean or replace the air filter.

## 309 · Machine device not answering {#c309}

**Class:** [Alarm](codes.md#class-alarm) · **Place:** the device.

**What you see.** The alarm window with **“Connection lost:”** followed by the name of the device, for example the hopper. Its tile has a grey ring.

**What to do:**

1. Check the cable of the named device to the HUB-8.
2. Check the power and the cable of the HUB-8 itself, if all its devices are silent.

## 310 · Wrong device on a HUB-8 input {#c310}

**Class:** [Alarm](codes.md#class-alarm) · **Place:** the device.

**What you see.** The alarm window with **“Wrong device type:”** followed by the name of the device. Its tile shows **“Wrong”**.

**What to do:**

1. Check that the device is wired to its own input.
2. Check that the kind of the device is right in the machine's devices: [HUB-8 inputs](hub8-inputs.md).

## 311 · Tractor input in alarm {#c311}

**Class:** [Alarm](codes.md#class-alarm) · **Place:** the device.

**What you see.** The alarm window with **“Alarm:”** followed by the name of the device.

**What to do:**

1. Check the device named in the window.


# 4xx · Tramline actuators

Codes 4xx come from the tramline actuators. The window names the device **“Tramline actuator”** and gives its number, for example “#1”. How the tramline is set up: [Tramline](tramline.md).

How to read a code, the four classes and how each looks in the app: [How service codes work](codes.md).

## 401 · Tramline actuator not answering {#c401}

**Class:** [Alarm](codes.md#class-alarm) · **Place:** the tramline actuator.

**What you see.** The alarm window with **“Connection lost”**, **“Tramline actuator”** and its number.

**What to do:**

1. Check the cable and the power of the tramline actuator.

## 402 · Not a tramline actuator {#c402}

**Class:** [Device fault](codes.md#class-fault) · **Place:** the tramline actuator.

**What you see.** The alarm window with an orange title, **“Wrong device type!”**, **“Tramline actuator”** and its number. It comes at once, without delay.

**What to do:**

1. Another device answers in the place of this actuator: check the numbering of the devices on the machine.

## 403 · Tramline actuator position unknown {#c403}

**Class:** [Device fault](codes.md#class-fault) · **Place:** the tramline actuator.

**What you see.** The alarm window with an orange title, **“Unknown state”**, **“Tramline actuator”** and its number.

**What to do:**

1. Check the shutter mechanism.
2. Open **“Settings”** › **“Machine”** › the actuator › **“Registers”** and press **“Reset”** to clear the state.

## 404 · Tramline actuator jammed {#c404}

**Class:** [Alarm](codes.md#class-alarm) · **Place:** the tramline actuator.

**What you see.** The alarm window with **“Jammed”**, **“Tramline actuator”** and its number.

**What to do:**

1. Free the shutter mechanism.
2. Open **“Settings”** › **“Machine”** › the actuator › **“Registers”** and press **“Reset”** to clear the state.


# 6xx · Gateway and link

Codes 6xx are about the gateway and the radio link between the gateway and the iPad or iPhone. While the link is down, every figure on the screen is old: the screen is dimmed and the alarms of the rows wait.

How to read a code, the four classes and how each looks in the app: [How service codes work](codes.md).

## 601 · Link to the gateway lost {#c601}

**Class:** [Alarm](codes.md#class-alarm) · **Place:** none.

**What you see.** The alarm window with **“Bridge link lost”**, after the link has been down for 3 seconds. A red capsule in the middle of the screen says what the app is doing, for example **“Looking for the bridge…”**. The window closes by itself when the gateway answers again.

**What to do:**

1. Check that the gateway has power.
2. Check that the iPad or iPhone is still in the cab, close to the gateway.
3. Wait: the app reconnects by itself. If it does not, use **“Reconnect”** in **“Settings”** › **“Machine”** › **“Bridge”**.

## 602 · Gateway silent {#c602}

**Class:** [Alarm](codes.md#class-alarm) · **Place:** none.

**What you see.** The red capsule **“Bridge is silent…”**: the link is there, but no data comes. The screen is dimmed; after 3 seconds the window **“Bridge link lost”** opens as for code 601.

**What to do:**

1. Wait 10 seconds.
2. If it stays, switch the power of the gateway off and on.


# 7xx · iPad and iPhone

Codes 7xx are about the iPad or iPhone that runs the Hectare app: things the tablet does that would hide an alarm or stop the app from reaching the gateway.

How to read a code, the four classes and how each looks in the app: [How service codes work](codes.md).

## 701 · Tablet volume off {#c701}

**Class:** [Attention](codes.md#class-attention) · **Place:** none.

**What you see.** The yellow capsule **“Volume is off”** at the top of the screen and in the alarm window. The media volume of the tablet is below 20 %: the buzzer runs, but nobody hears it.

**What to do:**

1. Turn the volume of the tablet up with its volume buttons. The side switch does not silence the alarm; the volume does.

## 702 · Sound goes to headphones {#c702}

**Class:** [Attention](codes.md#class-attention) · **Place:** none.

**What you see.** The yellow capsule **“Sound in headphones”**: the sound goes to headphones, a Bluetooth speaker, AirPlay or a car system, not to the tablet's own speaker.

**What to do:**

1. Disconnect the headphones or the external audio so that the buzzer plays from the tablet.

## 703 · No GNSS speed {#c703}

**Class:** [Attention](codes.md#class-attention) · **Place:** none.

**What you see.** The words **“no speed”** where the speed is shown (the speed sheet, **“GNSS speed”** in **“Settings”** › **“Machine”** › **“Bridge”**). No fresh speed for 2 seconds: Hybrid and Precision cannot judge the rows. No window opens.

**What to do:**

1. Move out under the open sky.
2. Check that the app may use the location: iPad Settings › Privacy & Security › Location Services › Hectare.
3. Check that this iPad has GNSS: Hybrid and Precision need an iPad with GNSS (Cellular).

## 704 · Bluetooth off {#c704}

**Class:** [Alarm](codes.md#class-alarm) · **Place:** none.

**What you see.** The red capsule **“Bluetooth is off”** in the middle of the screen. The app cannot reach the gateway.

**What to do:**

1. Switch Bluetooth on in the tablet's Control Centre or Settings.

## 705 · Bluetooth not allowed {#c705}

**Class:** [Alarm](codes.md#class-alarm) · **Place:** none.

**What you see.** The red capsule **“No Bluetooth permission”** in the middle of the screen. The app may not use Bluetooth and cannot reach the gateway.

**What to do:**

1. Allow Bluetooth for the app: iPad Settings › Hectare › Bluetooth.


# 8xx · Gateway update

Codes 8xx belong to the update of the gateway's firmware from the app. The update screen shows the code in front of the result, for example “804 · Bridge updated”. How to run the update: [Update the gateway](bridge-update.md).

How to read a code, the four classes and how each looks in the app: [How service codes work](codes.md).

## 801 · Update transfer started {#c801}

**Class:** [Record](codes.md#class-record) · **Place:** none.

**What you see.** On the update screen this is the start of the stage **“Firmware transfer”**; no code is shown. The gateway keeps it as a record.

**What to do.** Nothing. This code is a record for the service.

## 802 · Update transferred in full {#c802}

**Class:** [Record](codes.md#class-record) · **Place:** none.

**What you see.** On the update screen this is the end of the stage **“Firmware transfer”**, after which the screen moves on to **“Bridge restart”**; no code is shown. The gateway keeps it as a record. The image is transferred and accepted; its signature is checked later, when the gateway switches to it, and a refusal then comes as [806](codes-8-gateway-update.md#c806).

**What to do.** Nothing. This code is a record for the service.

## 803 · Update activated {#c803}

**Class:** [Record](codes.md#class-record) · **Place:** none.

**What you see.** On the update screen this is the stage **“Bridge restart”**; no code is shown. The gateway keeps it as a record of its restart onto the new firmware.

**What to do:**

1. Wait up to a minute and do not switch the gateway off.

## 804 · Gateway updated {#c804}

**Class:** [Record](codes.md#class-record) · **Place:** none.

**What you see.** On the update screen: **“804 · Bridge updated”** and **“The new firmware passed its check and runs. The monitor works as before.”**

**What to do.** Nothing. This code is a record for the service.

## 805 · Gateway went back to the previous firmware {#c805}

**Class:** [Attention](codes.md#class-attention) · **Place:** none.

**What you see.** On the update screen: **“805 · The bridge went back to its previous firmware”**. The new firmware failed its own check; the gateway runs the previous one and works.

**What to do:**

1. Go on working.
2. Tell the service the code.

## 806 · Firmware refused: signature {#c806}

**Class:** [Attention](codes.md#class-attention) · **Place:** none.

**What you see.** On the update screen: **“806 · The bridge refused the firmware: the signature does not match”**. The gateway keeps its firmware.

**What to do:**

1. Update the Hectare app and try again.
2. If it repeats, tell the service the code.

## 807 · Firmware refused: not newer {#c807}

**Class:** [Record](codes.md#class-record) · **Place:** none.

**What you see.** On the update screen: **“807 · The bridge refused the firmware: it is not newer”** and **“The bridge runs its own firmware. Nothing to do.”**

**What to do.** Nothing. This code is a record for the service.

## 808 · Update transfer interrupted {#c808}

**Class:** [Attention](codes.md#class-attention) · **Place:** none.

**What you see.** On the update screen: **“808 · Firmware transfer interrupted”**. The gateway runs its previous firmware.

**What to do:**

1. Keep the tablet close to the gateway.
2. Start the update again; the transfer starts from the beginning.

## 809 · Update not possible now {#c809}

**Class:** [Attention](codes.md#class-attention) · **Place:** none.

**What you see.** On the update screen: **“809 · The bridge is busy: no update now”**, or **“809 · The machine is seeding: the update did not start”**. Nothing was sent.

**What to do:**

1. Finish seeding and stop the machine.
2. Clear the active alarm on the seeder.
3. Wait a minute and try again.

## 810 · Gateway did not come back after the restart {#c810}

**Class:** [Attention](codes.md#class-attention) · **Place:** none.

**What you see.** On the update screen: **“810 · The bridge did not come back after the restart”**. The app waited 2 minutes for the gateway after its restart.

**What to do:**

1. Check the power of the gateway and wait a minute.
2. If it is still not back, switch the power of the gateway off and on and open the update screen again.


# 9xx · Setup answers of the gateway

Codes 9xx are the gateway's answers when the app writes something to it: the machine profile, a setting of a row group, the rate, or the number of a sensor. In this pre-release version the app shows a number after the words **“the bridge answered with code”**, after **“Error #”**, or at the end of a message such as **“write interrupted (code”**. Add 900 to that number to get the service code: “code 13” is 913. Some answers have their own words; they are given below.

How to read a code, the four classes and how each looks in the app: [How service codes work](codes.md).

## 901 · Setup data damaged on the way {#c901}

**Class:** [Attention](codes.md#class-attention) · **Place:** none.

**What you see.** In the profile status line: **“the bridge rejected the profile (checksum)”**. Elsewhere: “code 1”.

**What to do:**

1. Write again, with the tablet close to the gateway.

## 902 · Profile too large for the gateway {#c902}

**Class:** [Attention](codes.md#class-attention) · **Place:** none.

**What you see.** In the profile status line: **“too many rows for the bridge (up to”** and the largest number of rows.

**What to do:**

1. Reduce the number of rows and devices in the machine profile.

## 903 · Gateway does not know a channel role {#c903}

**Class:** [Attention](codes.md#class-attention) · **Place:** none.

**What you see.** In the profile status line: **“the bridge doesn't understand this profile (code”** 3).

**What to do:**

1. Bring the app and the gateway firmware to the same version: update the app, then update the gateway.
2. Tell the service the code.

## 904 · Gateway does not know a measured kind {#c904}

**Class:** [Attention](codes.md#class-attention) · **Place:** none.

**What you see.** In the profile status line: **“the bridge doesn't understand this profile (code”** 4).

**What to do:**

1. Bring the app and the gateway firmware to the same version: update the app, then update the gateway.
2. Tell the service the code.

## 905 · Gateway could not save {#c905}

**Class:** [Attention](codes.md#class-attention) · **Place:** none.

**What you see.** In the profile status line: **“the bridge could not save the profile”**.

**What to do:**

1. Write again.
2. If it repeats, tell the service the code.

## 906 · Write broken off {#c906}

**Class:** [Attention](codes.md#class-attention) · **Place:** none.

**What you see.** In the profile status line: **“write interrupted (code”** 6).

**What to do:**

1. Write again, with the tablet close to the gateway.

## 907 · Gateway does not know the command {#c907}

**Class:** [Attention](codes.md#class-attention) · **Place:** none.

**What you see.** **“the bridge answered with code”** 7, or **“Error #”**7.

**What to do:**

1. Bring the app and the gateway firmware to the same version: update the app, then update the gateway.
2. Tell the service the code.

## 908 · Profile version not supported {#c908}

**Class:** [Attention](codes.md#class-attention) · **Place:** none.

**What you see.** In the profile status line: **“the bridge doesn't understand this profile (code”** 8).

**What to do:**

1. Bring the app and the gateway firmware to the same version: update the app, then update the gateway.
2. Tell the service the code.

## 909 · Setup data came too fast {#c909}

**Class:** [Attention](codes.md#class-attention) · **Place:** none.

**What you see.** In the profile status line: **“write interrupted (code”** 9).

**What to do:**

1. Write again, with the tablet close to the gateway.

## 910 · Write timed out {#c910}

**Class:** [Attention](codes.md#class-attention) · **Place:** none.

**What you see.** In the profile status line: **“write interrupted (code”** 10).

**What to do:**

1. Write again, with the tablet close to the gateway.

## 911 · Gateway does not know the device data {#c911}

**Class:** [Attention](codes.md#class-attention) · **Place:** none.

**What you see.** In the profile status line: **“the bridge doesn't understand this profile (code”** 11).

**What to do:**

1. Bring the app and the gateway firmware to the same version: update the app, then update the gateway.
2. Tell the service the code.

## 912 · Gateway busy: seeding or another operation {#c912}

**Class:** [Attention](codes.md#class-attention) · **Place:** none.

**What you see.** **“bridge busy: seeding under way”** in the profile status line; **“Bridge busy: seed is still flowing. Stop the seeder and retry in a minute.”** or **“Seed is still flowing — the bridge does not listen to the bus. Stop the seeder.”** when numbering a sensor.

**What to do:**

1. Stop seeding, or wait until the other setup operation is finished.
2. Try again.

## 913 · Sensor did not answer during numbering {#c913}

**Class:** [Attention](codes.md#class-attention) · **Place:** none.

**What you see.** When numbering a sensor: **“No connection”** followed by **“at step:”** and the step, for example **“saving”**.

**What to do:**

1. Check that the sensor is connected and that the sensor line has power.
2. Try again.

## 914 · More than one new sensor answered {#c914}

**Class:** [Attention](codes.md#class-attention) · **Place:** none.

**What you see.** When numbering a sensor: **“More than one device on the network!”**

**What to do:**

1. Leave only one new sensor connected.
2. Try again.

## 915 · Sensor refused the number {#c915}

**Class:** [Attention](codes.md#class-attention) · **Place:** none.

**What you see.** When numbering a sensor: **“Error #”**15 followed by the step.

**What to do:**

1. Try again.
2. If it repeats, tell the service the code and the number of the sensor.

## 916 · Number outside the allowed range {#c916}

**Class:** [Attention](codes.md#class-attention) · **Place:** none.

**What you see.** When numbering a sensor: **“Number outside 1…199”**; the button stays off.

**What to do:**

1. Choose a number in the allowed range — the number the app offers for the row.

## 917 · Gateway busy with another sensor operation {#c917}

**Class:** [Attention](codes.md#class-attention) · **Place:** none.

**What you see.** When numbering a sensor: **“The bridge is busy with another action, please wait.”**

**What to do:**

1. Wait until the current operation with the sensors is finished.
2. Try again.

## 918 · Row group setting refused {#c918}

**Class:** [Attention](codes.md#class-attention) · **Place:** none.

**What you see.** **“the bridge answered with code”** 18.

**What to do:**

1. Bring the app and the gateway firmware to the same version: update the app, then update the gateway.
2. Tell the service the code.

## 919 · Control mode refused {#c919}

**Class:** [Attention](codes.md#class-attention) · **Place:** none.

**What you see.** **“the bridge answered with code”** 19.

**What to do:**

1. Bring the app and the gateway firmware to the same version: update the app, then update the gateway.
2. Tell the service the code.

## 920 · Sensor number already taken {#c920}

**Class:** [Attention](codes.md#class-attention) · **Place:** none.

**What you see.** When numbering a sensor: **“Address taken”** — another sensor already answers on that number; the button stays off. Or **“Address 7 already used!”** (with your number) when the gateway finds the number taken.

**What to do:**

1. Choose a free number.
2. Or first give the sensor that holds this number another number.

## 921 · Motor setting refused {#c921}

**Class:** [Attention](codes.md#class-attention) · **Place:** none.

**What you see.** **“the bridge answered with code”** 21.

**What to do:**

1. Bring the app and the gateway firmware to the same version: update the app, then update the gateway.
2. Tell the service the code.
